action: Prescribe chronic anticoagulant therapy for HF patients with AF and elevated CHA2DS2-VASc score
action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >=2 (men) or >=3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention
source_text: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (for men) and >= 3 (for women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Prescribe DOAC over Warfarin for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF and permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. DOACs have fixed dosing, fewer drug-drug interactions, and no need for routine anticoagulation monitoring. In meta-analysis, DOACs more effectively reduced stroke/systemic embolism, major bleeding, and intracranial bleeding compared with warfarin.

properties.context: preferred over warfarin in HF patients

source_text: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. (Class I, LOE A)

action: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs in the polypharmacy setting of HF
action_detail: The guideline notes that DOACs have fewer drug-drug interactions than warfarin, which simplifies management in HF patients who typically require polypharmacy (beta blockers, ACEi/ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, diuretics, amiodarone, digoxin). Warfarin's narrow therapeutic index and CYP2C9/VKORC1-mediated metabolism make it susceptible to interactions with amiodarone, which is commonly used for AF rhythm control in HF. Warfarin may still be preferred when DOAC interactions or cost are concerns.

properties.mechanism: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs due to CYP-mediated metabolism and narrow therapeutic index
properties.clinical_effect: DOACs preferred due to fewer interactions in polypharmacy HF setting
properties.management: Consider DOAC over warfarin; if warfarin chosen, monitor INR closely especially with concomitant amiodarone or other CYP inhibitors

source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF (Class I, LOE A)

action: Warfarin interacts with Amiodarone requiring dose adjustment and closer INR monitoring
action_detail: The guideline discusses amiodarone as a rhythm control agent for AF in HF (AATAC trial) and separately notes warfarin's susceptibility to drug-drug interactions as a reason to prefer DOACs. Amiodarone is a potent CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor that increases warfarin levels by 30-50%, raising bleeding risk. When both are co-prescribed in HF+AF patients, warfarin dose should be reduced by 30-50% and INR monitored more frequently.

properties.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, reducing warfarin metabolism and increasing anticoagulant effect
properties.clinical_effect: Increased INR and bleeding risk; warfarin levels increase 30-50%
properties.management: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% when initiating amiodarone; increase INR monitoring frequency

source_text: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions (the DOAC are generally preferred)

action: Warfarin interacts with Digoxin requiring monitoring
action_detail: In HF patients with AF requiring both rate control (digoxin) and anticoagulation (warfarin), the two drugs may interact. Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index and warfarin-digoxin co-administration may modestly alter digoxin clearance. More importantly, both drugs require careful monitoring in the polypharmacy HF setting the guideline describes. The guideline's preference for DOAC over warfarin partly reflects the complexity of managing warfarin alongside other HF medications including digoxin.

properties.mechanism: Both have narrow therapeutic indices; co-administration in polypharmacy HF setting increases monitoring burden
properties.clinical_effect: Increased complexity of anticoagulation management; potential for altered digoxin or warfarin levels
properties.management: Monitor INR and digoxin levels; consider DOAC instead of warfarin to simplify regimen

source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF

action: AF ablation is reasonable for symptom improvement in HF patients
action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, catheter ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and quality of life. In AATAC trial (persistent AF, LVEF <40%, NYHA II-III), ablation improved sinus rhythm maintenance vs amiodarone with 45% decrease in hospitalization and lower mortality. In CASTLE-AF trial (AF, LVEF <35%, NYHA II-IV), ablation reduced composite of death/rehospitalization (28.5% vs 44.6%).

properties.context: in HF patients with AF-related symptoms

source_text: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation is reasonable when rhythm/rate control fails in AF with LVEF <=50%
action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <=50%, if rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, atrioventricular nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. CRT produced more benefit than RV pacing in trials (PAVE, BLOCK-HF).

properties.context: after AV nodal ablation when rate/rhythm control fails, LVEF <=50%

source_text: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if a rhythm control strategy fails or is not desired, and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, AV nodal ablation with implantation of a CRT device is reasonable. (Class IIa, LOE B-R)

action: Chronic anticoagulation is reasonable for HF patients with AF even without additional CHA2DS2-VASc risk factors
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF and permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, chronic anticoagulant therapy is reasonable for men and women without additional risk factors beyond HF. HF is a hypercoagulable state and independent risk factor for stroke, systemic embolism, and mortality in AF. Patients with HF and CHA2DS2-VASc of 1 with AF had 3-fold higher stroke risk than those without AF.
source_text: For patients with chronic HF and permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, chronic anticoagulant therapy is reasonable for men and women without additional risk factors. (Class IIa, LOE B-NR)
